messages:
Ria: Heads-up — after the 3.2.1 console canary I'm seeing rows from other orgs in the Insights panel for some users.
Mike: whoa, can you reproduce reliably?
Ria: yes — quick steps: login as user A (org A), open Insights -> recent queries, sometimes shows rows with org_id=B. Happens within 10s of switching org in the topbar.
Sam: that's bad. Any affected customers reported?
Ria: flagged by QA and one internal demo customer. Not public but we should treat as P1 for canary.
Anya: deploy-bot shows the canary latest rolled around 1795512000, route-affinity enabled on gateway. Could be a sticky header issue.
deploy-bot: deploy 3.2.1-canary -> web-console-group-2 completed at 1795512005 :rocket:
Mike: possible suspects: prefetch cache keyed without org header, or header mutated during rapid org swap. Check middleware that sets request.orgContext.
Sam: looked at logs: got this snippet from the panel API: `GET /api/insights?user=123 & cookie=session=xyz` — downstream query used org_id from session cache (org=A) but metadata on rows returned include org_id=B.
Ria: attaching repro curl from my session: ```curl -H "X-Org-ID: A" -b "session=xyz" https://console/api/insights``` response body includes rows: "org_id":"B".
Anya: hmm. Our router sets X-Org-ID from the topbar js. But we also have internal proxy that may rewrite headers when using the quick-switch shim. Could be header strip+reuse race.
Sam: I dug into the server-cache layer — prefix cache key is `insights:v1:user:<user_id>:query:<hash>` but it does NOT include active_org or X-Org-ID. So cache hits can return rows from previous org.
Mike: confirmed — cache key missing org scoping. That explains cross-tenant rows after a fast org switch.
Ria: is this only a UI cache or also edge/gateway level?
Sam: both. There's a small LRU in the web process and a shared memcached layer. Neither included org in key.
Anya: patch idea: include resolved_org.id in cache key everywhere and make cache entries explicit about org. Also invalidate on org switch for user-scoped caches.
Mike: agreed. We should also add a telemetry rate & a regression monitor: count of results where row.org_id != request.org. Alert if >0.1% over 5m.
Ria: good call — can we add a quick patch to rollback the canary while we fix?
Anya: yes. Rolling back group-2 now. deploy-bot: rollback 3.2.1-canary from web-console-group-2 initiated at 1795512600.
deploy-bot: rollback completed at 1795512615 :white_check_mark:
Sam: I'll open a PR for the cache key fix and a unit test that swaps orgs fast to catch this.
Mike: also add an integration test in canary pipeline: synthetic org switch + validate no cross-org rows.
Ria: and add a one-off job to scan recent telemetry for violations so we can notify affected customers.
Anya: I'll also add a header-assert middleware in debug builds to 400 if `X-Org-ID` missing or inconsistent with session mapping, so we detect other places that don't set it.
Mike: timeline? Sam — can we get a PR today and a quick canary redeploy tomorrow?
Sam: yes, I'll push a fix in a couple hours. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/console/pull/4582
Ria: thanks. Also opening a support ticket template for CS to notify the demo customer if we find exposure.
DevExBot: Note added to runbook 'console-data-isolation' with steps: rollback, patch cache key, telemetry alert, support notify.
Anya: will schedule postmortem after root cause and fix are validated. For now marking incident P1 and blocking further canaries until gating tests added. :no_entry:
Mike: thanks all — keep this thread updated with PR and canary results.
Ria: will update with scan results and repro artifacts.
